planting.note: Divide rooted crowns in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained potting mix or garden soil in partial to full shade; grow outdoors year-round only in sheltered, frost-free sites, otherwise as a houseplant or seasonal hanging-basket fern.

directions: Dallas is a compact Boston fern selection grown chiefly because it holds up better in the lower humidity of ordinary indoor air than the classic 'Bostoniensis', shedding fewer leaflets when conditions turn dry. Its dense, arching fronds of finely divided pinnae are shorter and more tightly held than standard Boston fern, giving it a tidier, more tabletop-friendly scale for pots, hanging baskets, and mixed shade containers. Water to keep the soil consistently moist and provide bright indirect light indoors or filtered shade outdoors; even with its improved humidity tolerance, prolonged bone-dry air will still brown the frond tips. Divide congested crowns in spring to propagate, since named Boston fern selections do not come true from spores.

planting.note: Divide rooted crowns in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained potting mix or garden soil in partial to full shade; treat as a houseplant or seasonal hanging-basket fern outside the warmest, most sheltered frost-free gardens.

directions: Florida Ruffle is one of the long-popular named Boston fern selections grown for pinnae that are more finely cut and ruffled along their edges than the plain, broader-leaved 'Bostoniensis', giving the arching fronds a softer, more textured look. It shares the classic Boston fern's cascading habit and is grown the same way, as a shaded porch and hanging-basket plant outdoors in frost-free zones or as a houseplant elsewhere. Consistent moisture and high humidity are essential, since the finely divided foliage dries and browns faster than coarser-leaved Boston fern cultivars in dry indoor air. Propagate only by dividing the crown, as the ruffled frond form does not come true from spores.

planting.note: Divide rooted crowns in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained potting mix or garden soil in partial to full shade; grow as a houseplant or seasonal hanging-basket fern except in the mildest, most sheltered frost-free gardens.

directions: Tiger is grown for fronds that are far more heavily ruffled than the plain, flatter pinnae of the classic 'Bostoniensis' Boston fern, giving the whole plant a denser, more crimped and textured look even at a glance. It is otherwise managed like other Boston fern selections, cascading gracefully from a hanging basket or large pot in bright, filtered shade on a porch or patio during the warm season. Keep the soil evenly moist and the air humid, since the extra leaflet surface created by the ruffling browns and sheds quickly in dry conditions. Divide the crown to propagate, since this heavily textured sport will not reproduce true from spores.
